#Rental Share and Owner share of each Metropolis
```{r}
iris_with_population <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_IRIS_with_Population.shp")

france_rental <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/france_rental.csv")

top_100_cities <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/France_maps/metro/top_100_metro.shp")

# Perform the spatial join using 'st_join'
# This will match geometries based on spatial relationships
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population %>%
    left_join(france_rental, by = c("CODE_IR" = "IRIS"))


iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  select(-ends_with(".y")) %>%
  # Optionally, rename columns to remove the .x suffix if needed
  rename_with(~ gsub("\\.x$", "", .))

# Convert 'P21_PMEN' to numeric, and handle any coercion warnings
iris_with_population_and_rental$P21_PMEN <- as.numeric(iris_with_population_and_rental$P21_PMEN)

## Convert 'rental_sh' to numeric with proper handling
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(rental_sh = as.numeric(rental_sh))

# Ensure both datasets are data frames
iris_df <- st_drop_geometry(iris_with_population_and_rental)
metro_units_df <- st_drop_geometry(top_100_cities)

# Perform a standard join on the 'UU2020' column
france_metro_shares <- iris_df %>%
  right_join(metro_units_df, by = "codgeo") %>%
  group_by(codgeo, libgeo.x) %>%
  summarise(
    metro_rental_share = mean(rental_sh, na.rm = TRUE),
    metro_owner_share = 100 - metro_rental_share
  )

# View the resulting summarization
print(france_metro_shares)
```

```{r}
# Calculating rental share and owner share
france_metro_shares <- iris_df %>%
  right_join(metro_units_df %>% select(codgeo, libgeo), by = "codgeo") %>%
  group_by(codgeo, libgeo.x) %>%  # Ensure `libgeo` is retained
  summarise(
    metro_rental_share = mean(rental_sh, na.rm = TRUE),
    metro_owner_share = 100 - metro_rental_share,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  left_join(france_metro_shares, by = "codgeo")

iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(rental_sh = as.numeric(rental_sh))

library(data.table)

# Convert to data.table
iris_dt <- as.data.table(iris_with_population_and_rental)
metro_dt <- as.data.table(metro_units_df)

# Ensure rental_sh is numeric to avoid errors
iris_dt[, rental_sh := as.numeric(rental_sh)]

# Calculate owner share and divergence value efficiently
iris_dt[, owner_sh := 100 - rental_sh]
iris_dt[, divergence_value := rental_sh * log(rental_sh / metro_rental_share) + 
                         owner_sh * log(owner_sh / metro_owner_share), 
        by = codgeo]

# Aggregate at metro level (codgeo) using fast data.table operations
metro_divergence <- iris_dt[, .(avg_divergence_value = mean(divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE)), by = codgeo]

# Merge with metro information
metro_divergence <- metro_dt[, .(codgeo, libgeo)][metro_divergence, on = "codgeo"]

# Print final result
print(metro_divergence)
```

#Mapping Metropolis-Level Divergence Index Values for Housing Tenure#
```{r}
# Inmport france boundaries
france_boundaries <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/France_maps/metro/france_boundary.shp")

# Calculating rental share and owner share
france_metro_shares <- iris_df %>%
  right_join(metro_units_df %>% select(codgeo, libgeo), by = "codgeo") %>%
  group_by(codgeo, libgeo.x) %>%  # Ensure `libgeo` is retained
  summarise(
    metro_rental_share = mean(rental_sh, na.rm = TRUE),
    metro_owner_share = 100 - metro_rental_share,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  left_join(france_metro_shares, by = "codgeo")

iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(rental_sh = as.numeric(rental_sh))

# Join the data sets based on proper column names, ensuring all are data frames
divergence_values <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  # ✅ Bring in metro_rental_share and metro_owner_share first
  left_join(france_metro_shares %>% select(codgeo, metro_rental_share, metro_owner_share),
            by = "codgeo") %>%
  mutate(
    owner_sh = 100 - rental_sh,
    divergence_value = (
      rental_sh * log(rental_sh / metro_rental_share) +
      owner_sh * log(owner_sh / metro_owner_share)
    )
  ) %>%
  select(libgeo, codgeo, IRIS, UU2020, CODE_IR, rental_sh, owner_sh, divergence_value)

# Summarizing divergence_values at the metro level by averaging divergence values
metro_divergence <- divergence_values %>%
  group_by(codgeo) %>%
  summarize(
    libgeo = first(libgeo),
    avg_divergence_value = mean(divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Convert metro_divergence to a regular data frame if needed
metro_divergence <- as.data.frame(metro_divergence)

# Join the metro divergence data with the metro shapefile
map_data_metro <- top_100_cities %>%
  dplyr::left_join(metro_divergence, by = c("codgeo" = "codgeo"))

# Check and filter out areas with NA divergence values if necessary
map_data_metro <- map_data_metro %>%
  filter(!is.na(avg_divergence_value))

# Ensure CRS (Coordinate Reference System) Matches
st_crs(map_data_metro) <- st_crs(france_boundaries)

# Proceed with calculating breaks and plotting
breaks_metro <- unique(quantile(map_data_metro$avg_divergence_value, probs = seq(0, 1, 0.25), na.rm = TRUE))

if (length(breaks_metro) < 5) {
  breaks_metro <- seq(min(map_data_metro$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
                      max(map_data_metro$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE),
                      length.out = 5)
}

map_data_metro <- map_data_metro %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_category = cut(
      avg_divergence_value,
      breaks = breaks_metro,
      labels = c("Least Divergent", "Second Quartile", "Third Quartile", "Most Divergent"),
      include.lowest = TRUE,
      right = FALSE
    )
  )

# Plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = france_boundaries, fill = NA, color = "gray", size = 0.5) +  # France boundaries
  geom_sf(data = map_data_metro, aes(fill = divergence_category)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Least Divergent" = "#c6dbef", 
                               "Second Quartile" = "#9ecae1", 
                               "Third Quartile" = "#6baed6", 
                               "Most Divergent" = "#3182bd"),
                    na.value = "grey50", 
                    name = "Divergence Index\nValue (Quartile)") +
  labs(title = "Metro-Level Divergence Index Values for Housing Tenure") +
  theme_minimal()
```
#
```{r}
# Load and prepare the shapefile with polygons
iris_with_boundaries <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_Combined_Data.shp")

# Compute divergence values
# Ensure metro shares are available before computing divergence
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  left_join(
    france_metro_shares %>% select(codgeo, metro_rental_share, metro_owner_share),
    by = "codgeo"
  )

# Compute divergence values
divergence_values <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(
    rental_sh    = as.numeric(rental_sh),
    owner_sh     = 100 - rental_sh,
    divergence_value = ifelse(
      rental_sh > 0 & owner_sh > 0 & metro_rental_share > 0 & metro_owner_share > 0,
      rental_sh * log(rental_sh / metro_rental_share) +
      owner_sh  * log(owner_sh  / metro_owner_share),
      NA_real_
    )
  ) %>%
  select(libgeo, IRIS, UU2020, CODE_IR, rental_sh, owner_sh, divergence_value) 

# Convert necessary datasets to data frames
top_100_cities_df <- as.data.frame(top_100_cities)
divergence_values_df <- as.data.frame(divergence_values)

# Merge divergence data with IRIS boundaries
iris_data <- iris_with_boundaries %>%
  left_join(divergence_values_df, by = "CODE_IR")

# Compute divergence categories once for all cities
iris_data <- iris_data %>%
  group_by(libgeo) %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_category = case_when(
      divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Most Divergent",
      divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Third Quartile",
      divergence_value >= quantile(divergence_value, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "Second Quartile",
      TRUE ~ "Least Divergent"
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Filter only the top 100 cities by libgeo
iris_data_top100 <- iris_data %>%
  filter(libgeo %in% top_100_cities_df$libgeo)

# Set the folder path where images will be saved
output_folder <- "C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/image/"

# Create and save individual maps for each of the top 100 cities
for (city_name in unique(iris_data_top100$libgeo)) {
  city_data <- iris_data_top100 %>% filter(libgeo == city_name)
  
  city_plot <- ggplot(data = city_data) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = divergence_category), color = "black", size = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Least Divergent" = "#c6dbef", 
                                 "Second Quartile" = "#9ecae1", 
                                 "Third Quartile" = "#6baed6", 
                                 "Most Divergent" = "#3182bd"),
                      na.value = "grey70", 
                      name = "Divergence Category") +
    labs(title = paste("Divergence Index Map for", city_name)) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
          axis.text = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks = element_blank())

  # Define output file name
  output_file <- file.path(output_folder, paste0("Divergence_Map_", gsub(" ", "_", city_name), ".jpg"))

  # Save the map as a .jpg file
  ggsave(filename = output_file, plot = city_plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300, device = "jpeg")
  
  print(paste("Saved:", output_file))  # Print progress
}
```

```{r}
# Set the folder path where the images will be saved

  mutate(divergence_category = case_when(
    divergence_quartile == 4 & rental_sh > owner_sh ~ "Most Divergent, High-Rental",
```

```{r}
# Load income data
income_data <- read_csv("/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/Updated_IRIS_with_Income.csv")

# Categorize IRISs into income brackets based on median income
income_data <- income_data %>%
  mutate(
    income_category = case_when(
      DEC_MED21 < 20000 ~ "Lower",
      DEC_MED21 >= 20000 & DEC_MED21 < 40000 ~ "Middle",
      DEC_MED21 >= 40000 ~ "Higher"
    )
  )

# Calculate the share of each category per metro
income_shares <- income_data %>%
  group_by(codgeo, income_category) %>%
  summarize(count = n()) %>%
  group_by(codgeo) %>%
  mutate(
    share = count / sum(count)
  ) %>%
  select(codgeo, income_category, share)

# Calculate metro-level shares for income categories
metro_shares <- income_shares %>%
  group_by(income_category) %>%
  summarize(metro_share = mean(share, na.rm = TRUE))

# Calculate income divergence index
income_divergence <- income_shares %>%
  left_join(metro_shares, by = "income_category") %>%
  mutate(
    divergence_component = share * log(share / metro_share)
  ) %>%
  group_by(codgeo) %>%
  summarize(income_divergence_index = sum(divergence_component, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge with housing divergence
merged_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  left_join(income_divergence, by = "codgeo")

# Plotting the relationship
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_divergence_value, y = income_divergence_index)) +
  geom_point(color = "#4b0082", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Housing Divergence Index Value",
    y = "Income Divergence Index Value",
    title = "Housing Divergence vs. Income Segregation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Load metro shapefile
metro_shapefile <- st_read("C:/Users/ohdaw/OneDrive/Documents/R_Projects/rental_desert/France/France_maps/metro/top_100_metro.shp")

# Determine thresholds for high/low segregation
housing_threshold <- median(metro_divergence$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE)
income_threshold <- median(income_divergence$income_divergence_index, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a dataframe for segregation mapping
segregation_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  left_join(income_divergence, by = "codgeo") %>%
  mutate(
    segregation_type = case_when(
      avg_divergence_value >= housing_threshold & income_divergence_index >= income_threshold ~ "High Housing, High Income Segregation",
      avg_divergence_value >= housing_threshold & income_divergence_index < income_threshold ~ "High Housing, Low Income Segregation",
      avg_divergence_value < housing_threshold & income_divergence_index >= income_threshold ~ "Low Housing, High Income Segregation",
      TRUE ~ "Low Housing, Low Income Segregation"
    )
  )

# Ensure `segregation_data` is compatible for join
segregation_data_df <- as.data.frame(segregation_data)

# Join with the shapefile
map_data <- metro_shapefile %>%
  left_join(segregation_data_df, by = c("codgeo" = "codgeo"))

# Plot the map
ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(data = france_boundaries, fill = NA, color = "gray", size = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = segregation_type), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "High Housing, High Income Segregation" = "#6a51a3",
    "High Housing, Low Income Segregation" = "#9ecae1",
    "Low Housing, High Income Segregation" = "#807dba",
    "Low Housing, Low Income Segregation" = "#bcbddc"
  )) +
  labs(title = "Metro Areas with High Housing and High Income Segregation",
       fill = "Segregation Type") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Convert necessary columns to numeric
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(
    P21_RP_ACH19 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH19)),
    P21_RP_ACH45 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH45)),
    P21_RP_ACH70 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH70)),
    P21_RP_ACH90 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH90)),
    P21_RP_ACH05 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH05)),
    P21_RP_ACH18 = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACH18)),
    P21_RP_ACHTOT = as.numeric(as.character(P21_RP_ACHTOT))
  )

# Calculate the entropy index for building age
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(
    share_ACH19 = P21_RP_ACH19 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH45 = P21_RP_ACH45 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH70 = P21_RP_ACH70 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH90 = P21_RP_ACH90 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH05 = P21_RP_ACH05 / P21_RP_ACHTOT,
    share_ACH18 = P21_RP_ACH18 / P21_RP_ACHTOT
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    building_age_entropy_index = -(
      sum(
        c(share_ACH19, share_ACH45, share_ACH70, share_ACH90, share_ACH05, share_ACH18) * 
        log(c(share_ACH19, share_ACH45, share_ACH70, share_ACH90, share_ACH05, share_ACH18)), 
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# Load necessary library
library(data.table)

# Convert to data.table
iris_dt <- as.data.table(iris_with_population_and_rental)

# Compute building age divergence using fast data.table operations
building_age_divergence <- iris_dt[, .(
  building_age_divergence_index = mean(building_age_entropy_index, na.rm = TRUE)
), by = codgeo]

# Ensure building_age_divergence is a data frame
building_age_divergence_df <- as.data.frame(building_age_divergence)

# Merge with housing divergence
merged_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%  # Ensure metro_divergence is also a data frame
  left_join(building_age_divergence_df, by = "codgeo")

# Plotting the relationship
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_divergence_value, y = building_age_divergence_index)) +
  geom_point(color = "#4b0082", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Housing Divergence Index Value",
    y = "Building Age Entropy Index Value",
    title = "Housing Divergence vs. Building Age Segregation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Convert household size column to numeric if needed
iris_with_population_and_rental <- iris_with_population_and_rental %>%
  mutate(P21_NPER_RP = as.numeric(P21_NPER_RP))

# Convert to data.table
dt <- as.data.table(iris_with_population_and_rental)

# Compute share of each household size per metro
household_size_shares <- dt[, .(count = .N), by = .(codgeo, P21_NPER_RP)][
  , share := count / sum(count), by = codgeo
]

# Calculate the entropy index for household size distribution
household_size_entropy <- household_size_shares %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    entropy_component = ifelse(share > 0, share * log(share), 0)
  ) %>%
  group_by(codgeo) %>%
  summarize(household_size_divergence_index = -sum(entropy_component, na.rm = TRUE))

# Merge with housing divergence
merged_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  left_join(household_size_entropy, by = "codgeo")

# Plot the relationship
ggplot(merged_data, aes(x = avg_divergence_value, y = household_size_divergence_index)) +
  geom_point(color = "#4b0082", size = 3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE, color = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    x = "Housing Divergence Index Value",
    y = "Household Size Divergence Index",
    title = "Housing Divergence vs. Household Size Segregation"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
# Define thresholds for high/low segregation:
# (Assuming 'metro_divergence' contains the housing divergence index and 
# 'household_divergence' contains the household size divergence index)
housing_threshold   <- median(metro_divergence$avg_divergence_value, na.rm = TRUE)
household_threshold <- median(household_size_entropy$household_size_divergence_index, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create a dataframe for segregation mapping by merging the two divergence indexes.
# (Note: Adjust the join key if your metro identifier is different.)
segregation_data <- metro_divergence %>%
  left_join(household_size_entropy, by = "codgeo") %>%
  mutate(
    segregation_type = case_when(
      avg_divergence_value >= housing_threshold & household_size_divergence_index >= household_threshold ~ "High Housing, High Household Size Segregation",
      avg_divergence_value >= housing_threshold & household_size_divergence_index <  household_threshold ~ "High Housing, Low Household Size Segregation",
      avg_divergence_value <  housing_threshold & household_size_divergence_index >= household_threshold ~ "Low Housing, High Household Size Segregation",
      TRUE ~ "Low Housing, Low Household Size Segregation"
    )
  )

# Ensure the segregation data is a data frame
segregation_data_df <- as.data.frame(segregation_data)

# Join with your metro shapefile.
# (Here, it's assumed the shapefile has a metro identifier column named 'uu2020' that corresponds to 'UU2020'.)
map_data <- metro_shapefile %>%
  left_join(segregation_data_df, by = c("codgeo" = "codgeo"))

# Plot the map using the new household size segregation categories
ggplot(map_data) +
  geom_sf(data = france_boundaries, fill = NA, color = "gray", size = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = segregation_type), color = NA) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "High Housing, High Household Size Segregation" = "#6a51a3",
    "High Housing, Low Household Size Segregation" = "#9ecae1",
    "Low Housing, High Household Size Segregation" = "#807dba",
    "Low Housing, Low Household Size Segregation" = "#bcbddc"
  )) +
  labs(
    title = "Metro Areas with High Housing and High Household Size Segregation",
    fill = "Segregation Type"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
